rationale: The include-family tag has two real-world spellings and the lane knew only one. `!include` is not an Ansible tag at all — it belongs to third-party PyYAML extensions — and pyyaml-include 2.x, the current release, renamed it to `!inc`. The set of include tags was GUESSED rather than derived, and measuring it is what proved that: across all 9,953 files in the eight pinned corpora every spelling the lane originally knew occurs ZERO times, while the tags Ansible actually uses (`!vault` 30, `!unsafe` 31) are not in the set at all. So the gap could not be seen from the corpus and only a check of the libraries defining the construct exposed it. authoredBeforeAnalyzerRun is FALSE and that is recorded rather than glossed: this fixture was authored after the gap was found, from a documented library's published usage, which is a weaker form of independence than a pre-registered prediction.

expectImports.comment: `!inc`, the CURRENT pyyaml-include spelling, which the analyzer did not recognise before this fix. The LINE is pinned on the relationship rows below rather than here: this fixture's runner reads the ANALYZER result, where the field is `line_number`, while the production entry renames it to `line`. Pinning one spelling here would pass on the analyzer and fail the moment the shape is read at the seam, or the reverse. The relationship pin is the seam-independent place for it.
`!include`, the 1.x spelling, which the analyzer did recognise

forbidRelationships.note: THE NEGATIVE HALF, asserted by value. `!vault` annotates a value in place and names no file; if the include set were a substring or prefix rule this would be published as a file import, which is the over-firing class (Y24) rather than a missed edge.
`!unsafe` likewise annotates in place. Together with the row above this is what distinguishes a CLOSED set from a pattern match.

expectSymbols.name: secret
expectSymbols.comment: carries tagUri=vault and NO tagIncludePath — the assertion that a non-include tag stays a typed value

expectSymbols.name: modern
expectSymbols.comment: carries tagUri=inc AND tagIncludePath — the positive half of the same distinction

_shapesProbed.note: Probed directly against the analyzer before the expectation was written, because the fix widened a closed set and the failure mode of widening a set is over-firing, not under-firing. `!vault` and `!unsafe` record a tagUri and leave tagIncludePath undefined, so they stay typed values; `!inc` and `!include` both record tagIncludePath and emit an import with a 1-based line.

probed.list: [!inc .., !include ..]: both items import; the item path carries the sequence index
